definitionEn: To pass, send, or convey signals, data, cultural knowledge, or pathogens from one entity to another.
meaningVi: truyền tải, lây truyền
existingExample: Fibre-optic cables can transmit enormous volumes of digital information across continents with minimal latency.

definitionEn: Being the final, highest, or most fundamental goal, outcome, or authority in a process.
meaningVi: cuối cùng, tối thượng, căn bản nhất
existingExample: The ultimate objective of restorative justice is to reconcile offenders with affected communities.

definitionEn: Being the only one of its kind, or possessing distinctive traits unmatched elsewhere.
meaningVi: độc đáo, duy nhất, đặc thù
existingExample: Island archipelagos frequently harbour unique endemic species that have evolved in geographical isolation.

definitionEn: Capable of being seen by the eye, or clearly perceptible and evident in its effects.
meaningVi: có thể nhìn thấy, rõ rệt, hữu hình
existingExample: Retreating alpine glaciers provide some of the most visible evidence of anthropogenic climate change.

definitionEn: Done, given, or undertaken by free choice rather than legal obligation or financial compulsion.
meaningVi: tự nguyện, tình nguyện
existingExample: Critics argue that purely voluntary corporate sustainability pledges rarely yield substantial emission reductions.

definitionEn: To permanently give up a course of action, project, belief, or location.
meaningVi: từ bỏ, bỏ rơi, ngưng theo đuổi
existingExample: Prolonged droughts have forced thousands of rural farmers to abandon ancestral agricultural lands.

definitionEn: To occur simultaneously with, supplement, or go somewhere alongside another phenomenon or person.
meaningVi: đi kèm, đồng hành cùng
existingExample: Rapid urbanisation tends to accompany industrial expansion, placing immense strain on municipal water supplies.

definitionEn: To gradually gather, build up, or increase in quantity or concentration over time.
meaningVi: tích lũy, tích tụ dần
existingExample: Non-biodegradable microplastics readily accumulate within marine food webs, threatening apex predators.

definitionEn: Open to more than one interpretation, or lacking precision and clarity.
meaningVi: mơ hồ, đa nghĩa, không rõ ràng
existingExample: Poorly drafted legislation often contains ambiguous clauses that invite protracted courtroom disputes.

definitionEn: To add supplementary material, notes, or data to the end of a written document or record.
meaningVi: đính kèm, bổ sung vào cuối tài liệu
existingExample: Doctoral candidates are advised to append raw survey transcripts at the conclusion of their dissertations.

definitionEn: To recognise the full significance or complexity of something, or to increase in monetary value.
meaningVi: đánh giá đúng, trân trọng, tăng giá trị
existingExample: Interdisciplinary coursework enables engineering students to appreciate the ethical implications of emerging technologies.

definitionEn: Based on random choice or personal whim rather than consistent principle, logic, or empirical criteria.
meaningVi: tùy tiện, võ đoán, không có cơ sở hợp lý
existingExample: Setting an arbitrary age threshold for mandatory retirement disregards individual variations in cognitive vitality.

definitionEn: To systematically record, map, or trace the development and progression of trends or phenomena.
meaningVi: lập biểu đồ, ghi nhận tiến trình
existingExample: Demographers use census records to chart shifting fertility rates across post-industrial nations.

definitionEn: To make a complex concept, policy, or statement easier to understand and free from confusion.
meaningVi: làm rõ, giải thích minh bạch
existingExample: Regulatory authorities issued revised guidance to clarify how data protection laws apply to generative software.

definitionEn: A raw material, primary agricultural product, or valuable good that can be bought and sold on markets.
meaningVi: hàng hóa thiết yếu, thương phẩm
existingExample: Fresh potable water is increasingly treated as a scarce economic commodity rather than a universal human right.

definitionEn: To combine well with another element in a way that enhances or completes its qualities.
meaningVi: bổ sung, làm hoàn thiện thêm
existingExample: Qualitative interviews can effectively complement large-scale statistical surveys by uncovering underlying human motivations.

definitionEn: To comply with established rules, standards, or prevailing social norms and expectations.
meaningVi: tuân thủ, phù hợp với chuẩn mực
existingExample: All imported electrical appliances must conform to stringent European safety and efficiency standards.

definitionEn: Belonging to or occurring in the present era, or existing at the same historical time.
meaningVi: đương đại, hiện thời, cùng thời
existingExample: Contemporary urban architecture increasingly prioritises passive cooling and biophilic design principles.

definitionEn: To assert the opposite of a statement, or to be logically inconsistent with other evidence.
meaningVi: mâu thuẫn, phủ nhận, trái ngược với
existingExample: Recent archaeological excavations directly contradict earlier theories regarding prehistoric maritime trade routes.

definitionEn: An official system of money in general use within a country, or the state of being widely accepted.
meaningVi: tiền tệ, sự lưu hành phổ biến
existingExample: Persistent political instability frequently erodes investor confidence and triggers sharp depreciation of the national currency.

definitionEn: To serve as a formal sign, symbol, or literal designation for a particular concept or condition.
meaningVi: biểu thị, chỉ rõ, có nghĩa là
existingExample: In statistical charts, dashed trend lines typically denote projected figures rather than observed measurements.

definitionEn: To discover, identify, or perceive the presence of something subtle, hidden, or emerging.
meaningVi: phát hiện, nhận diện
existingExample: Satellite remote sensing enables conservationists to detect illegal deforestation in remote rainforests within hours.

definitionEn: To depart from an established course, standard procedure, statistical norm, or agreed plan.
meaningVi: chệch hướng, sai lệch so với chuẩn mực
existingExample: When actual consumer spending patterns deviate significantly from forecasts, central banks revise their monetary models.

definitionEn: A literary genre or theatrical art form written for performance, or a sequence of intense events.
meaningVi: kịch nghệ, nghệ thuật sân khấu
existingExample: Integrating classical drama into secondary curricula nurtures empathy, rhetorical poise, and critical literacy.

definitionEn: Occurring at the end of a long sequence of events, processes, or developments.
meaningVi: cuối cùng, sau cùng
existingExample: Unregulated aquifer depletion threatens the eventual collapse of irrigated agriculture in arid basins.

definitionEn: To publicly display an object, or to clearly manifest a particular trait, symptom, or behaviour.
meaningVi: thể hiện, biểu lộ, trưng bày
existingExample: Children raised in bilingual households frequently exhibit heightened executive function and cognitive flexibility.

definitionEn: To make full strategic use of a resource or opportunity, or to treat someone unfairly for personal gain.
meaningVi: khai thác triệt để, bóc lột
existingExample: Developing nations must establish equitable treaties to ensure multinational firms do not unfairly exploit local mineral reserves.

definitionEn: An official recommendation, general rule, or principle advising how an action should be carried out.
meaningVi: hướng dẫn, nguyên tắc chỉ đạo
existingExample: Each participating hospital adheres to a rigorous clinical guideline for administering antibiotic therapy.

definitionEn: To draw special attention to an important finding, issue, or feature.
meaningVi: làm nổi bật, nhấn mạnh
existingExample: Recent epidemiological reports highlight the stark correlation between chronic air pollution and respiratory illness.

definitionEn: Suggested, implied, or ingrained without being directly or explicitly articulated.
meaningVi: ngầm hiểu, hàm ẩn, tiềm ẩn
existingExample: Structured blind recruitment processes are designed to counteract implicit bias during candidate screening.

definitionEn: To bring about, trigger, or persuade a particular physiological, behavioural, or economic response.
meaningVi: gây ra, kích thích, thúc đẩy
existingExample: Prolonged exposure to artificial blue light before bedtime can induce severe circadian rhythm disruption.

definitionEn: Certain to happen and impossible to prevent or avoid under prevailing circumstances.
meaningVi: tất yếu, không thể tránh khỏi
existingExample: Given declining birth rates and rising life expectancy, demographic ageing appears virtually inevitable across East Asia.

definitionEn: To examine an object, facility, or process carefully to assess its quality, safety, or compliance.
meaningVi: kiểm tra kỹ lưỡng, thanh tra
existingExample: Independent structural engineers regularly inspect ageing suspension bridges to identify early signs of metal fatigue.

definitionEn: Of extreme force, concentration, degree, or emotional and intellectual seriousness.
meaningVi: mãnh liệt, gay gắt, cường độ cao
existingExample: Intense academic pressure among adolescents has prompted education ministries to reconsider high-stakes entrance examinations.

definitionEn: To reduce an undesirable effect, risk, or cost to the smallest possible extent.
meaningVi: giảm thiểu, hạ xuống mức thấp nhất
existingExample: Precision irrigation systems help farmers minimise water wastage while maintaining consistent crop yields.

definitionEn: Relating to the energy released by atomic nuclei, or referring to the core unit of a family or system.
meaningVi: thuộc về hạt nhân, nguyên tử
existingExample: Proponents contend that modern nuclear energy offers reliable low-carbon baseload power alongside wind and solar.

definitionEn: A distinct section of written discourse focused on a single coherent idea or argument.
meaningVi: đoạn văn
existingExample: In academic essays, each body paragraph should open with a clear topic sentence supported by empirical evidence.

definitionEn: A qualified professional actively engaged in an applied discipline such as medicine, law, or education.
meaningVi: người hành nghề chuyên môn (bác sĩ, luật sư...)
existingExample: Every healthcare practitioner is expected to stay abreast of peer-reviewed clinical advancements throughout their career.

definitionEn: Present as the strongest, most prevalent, or most influential element in a given context.
meaningVi: chiếm ưu thế, chủ đạo
existingExample: Fossil fuels remain the predominant source of global primary energy despite rapid renewable capacity growth.

definitionEn: The likelihood or anticipation of a future event, or the potential for future success.
meaningVi: triển vọng, viễn cảnh, khả năng xảy ra
existingExample: The prospect of widespread job displacement has spurred renewed debate over universal basic income schemes.

definitionEn: Relating to or affecting the fundamental nature of something; far-reaching and thorough.
meaningVi: triệt để, căn bản, cấp tiến
existingExample: Averting catastrophic warming demands radical transformations in global transport, agriculture, and heavy industry.

definitionEn: Made, selected, or occurring without deliberate pattern, bias, or conscious decision.
meaningVi: ngẫu nhiên
existingExample: Researchers selected a random sample of two thousand households to ensure nationally representative polling data.

definitionEn: To strengthen or support an existing belief, behaviour, structure, or social pattern.
meaningVi: củng cố, tăng cường, gia cố
existingExample: Algorithmic recommendation feeds can inadvertently reinforce existing cognitive biases by isolating users in echo chambers.

definitionEn: To return a damaged ecosystem, institution, confidence, or artefact to its former healthy or original condition.
meaningVi: khôi phục, phục hồi, tái thiết
existingExample: Coordinated wetland conservation projects aim to restore natural floodplains and revive endangered migratory bird populations.

definitionEn: To reconsider, alter, or update a text, estimate, curriculum, or policy in light of new information.
meaningVi: chỉnh sửa, sửa đổi, xem xét lại
existingExample: Economists had to revise their annual growth projections downward following unexpected global supply bottlenecks.

definitionEn: A structured timetable or procedural plan detailing when specific tasks or events are to take place.
meaningVi: lịch trình, kế hoạch thời gian
existingExample: Major public infrastructure projects frequently exceed their original budget and fall behind their projected schedule.

definitionEn: Characterised by anxiety, strained relations, or heightened anticipation of conflict.
meaningVi: căng thẳng, đầy áp lực
existingExample: Diplomatic negotiations over shared transboundary river basins remained exceptionally tense throughout the drought.

definitionEn: To bring a contract, agreement, process, or relationship to a formal and definitive end.
meaningVi: chấm dứt, kết thúc chính thức
existingExample: Either contracting party reserves the legal right to terminate the partnership in the event of material breach.

definitionEn: A recurring central idea, motif, or unifying concept explored in a discourse, work, or conference.
meaningVi: chủ đề xuyên suốt, đề tài chính
existingExample: Intergenerational equity emerged as the overarching theme of the international climate summit.

definitionEn: Remaining consistent and unvarying in form, standard, distribution, or quality across all cases.
meaningVi: đồng nhất, đồng đều, nhất quán
existingExample: Establishing uniform accounting standards across jurisdictions enhances transparency for international institutional investors.

definitionEn: A machine used for transporting people or goods, or a medium through which an idea or policy is conveyed.
meaningVi: phương tiện giao thông, công cụ truyền tải
existingExample: Subsidising electric vehicle adoption accelerates the decarbonisation of municipal public transport fleets.

definitionEn: Simulated or carried out via computer networks rather than physically, or being effectively so in practice.
meaningVi: ảo (trực tuyến), gần như thực tế
existingExample: Virtual laboratory simulations allow underfunded secondary schools to conduct complex chemistry experiments safely.

definitionEn: Relating to sight, perception by the eyes, or graphical representation of information.
meaningVi: thuộc thị giác, trực quan
existingExample: Effective visual data presentation enables policymakers to grasp multifaceted demographic shifts at a glance.

definitionEn: To adapt to or make space for different needs, demands, or a number of people.
meaningVi: đáp ứng, điều chỉnh để phù hợp; cung cấp chỗ ở
existingExample: Urban transport networks must be redesigned to accommodate the rapidly growing commuter population.

definitionEn: A comparison between two different things that highlights structural or functional similarities for explanation.
meaningVi: phép loại suy, sự tương đồng để so sánh giải thích
existingExample: The lecturer drew a compelling analogy between the human immune system and national cybersecurity defences.

definitionEn: To foresee a future event or problem and take appropriate action in advance.
meaningVi: dự đoán trước, lường trước và chuẩn bị ứng phó
existingExample: Policymakers failed to anticipate the long-term demographic pressures caused by declining birth rates.

definitionEn: To tell someone confidently that something is true or certain, or to make an outcome guaranteed.
meaningVi: cam đoan, bảo đảm, trấn an
existingExample: Strict regulatory audits are necessary to assure consumers that organic food labels are genuinely trustworthy.

definitionEn: To succeed in achieving a desired standard, goal, or level after sustained effort.
meaningVi: đạt được, giành được (mục tiêu, trình độ cao)
existingExample: Equitable funding enables students from underprivileged areas to attain higher academic qualifications.

definitionEn: The interest, representation, or benefit of a particular person, group, or organisation.
meaningVi: sự đại diện, lợi ích (thường dùng trong 'on behalf of')
existingExample: Environmental NGOs frequently lobby international summits on behalf of vulnerable coastal communities.

definitionEn: To bring or come to a complete end; to stop happening or operating.
meaningVi: ngừng, chấm dứt hoàn toàn
existingExample: Several heavy manufacturing plants were forced to cease operations after failing environmental inspections.

definitionEn: Logical, well-organised, and consistent so that parts fit together clearly as a whole.
meaningVi: mạch lạc, logic, gắn kết chặt chẽ
existingExample: Without a coherent national energy strategy, intermittent renewable subsidies yield disappointing results.

definitionEn: To occur at the same time as another event, or to agree closely in opinion or interest.
meaningVi: trùng hợp (về thời gian, quan điểm hoặc sự kiện)
existingExample: The sharpest decline in print newspaper readership appeared to coincide with the rise of smartphones.

definitionEn: To begin formally or officially, especially a project, legal proceeding, or academic term.
meaningVi: bắt đầu, khởi công, khởi sự (trang trọng)
existingExample: Construction of the high-speed railway is scheduled to commence following the final ecological review.

definitionEn: Able to exist, function, or be used together without conflict or technical difficulty.
meaningVi: tương thích, phù hợp, có thể cùng tồn tại
existingExample: Economists increasingly debate whether rapid GDP expansion is truly compatible with planetary ecological limits.

definitionEn: Happening, existing, or operating at the exact same time.
meaningVi: đồng thời, diễn ra cùng lúc
existingExample: Public hospitals struggled to cope with concurrent outbreaks of seasonal influenza and heat-related illness.

definitionEn: To keep or restrict someone or something within specific boundaries, limits, or areas.
meaningVi: giới hạn, thu hẹp phạm vi; giam giữ
existingExample: University curricula should not confine students to narrow vocational skills at the expense of critical inquiry.

definitionEn: Prolonged public disagreement or heated debate over a sensitive or disputed issue.
meaningVi: sự tranh cãi gay gắt, vấn đề gây tranh luận công khai
existingExample: The deployment of automated surveillance cameras in residential neighbourhoods sparked intense public controversy.

definitionEn: A statement, situation, or idea that is the exact opposite or reverse of another.
meaningVi: điều ngược lại, mệnh đề đảo
existingExample: While wealth can broaden educational access, the converse is not always true for emotional fulfilment.

definitionEn: A piece of mechanical or electronic equipment made for a specific purpose, or a rhetorical technique.
meaningVi: thiết bị, dụng cụ; thủ pháp (tu từ, kỹ thuật)
existingExample: Constant notifications from handheld devices can severely fragment adolescents' concentration during study.

definitionEn: To give a significant proportion of time, money, or effort to a particular purpose or cause.
meaningVi: dành trọn thời gian, nguồn lực, tâm huyết cho
existingExample: Governments ought to devote a larger share of healthcare budgets to preventive medicine rather than emergency care.

definitionEn: To become smaller, weaker, or less important, or to reduce the value or authority of something.
meaningVi: làm giảm bớt, suy giảm (giá trị, tầm quan trọng)
existingExample: Over-reliance on machine translation may gradually diminish learners' motivation to master foreign languages.

definitionEn: To twist facts, data, or perceptions out of their true or original state, often misleadingly.
meaningVi: bóp méo, xuyên tạc, làm sai lệch
existingExample: Selective reporting by partisan media outlets can systematically distort public perceptions of crime rates.

definitionEn: The length of time during which a process, condition, or event continues.
meaningVi: khoảng thời gian tồn tại, thời lượng
existingExample: Extending the duration of compulsory schooling has been linked to higher lifetime earnings across Europe.

definitionEn: To gradually wear away land, rock, or abstract qualities such as trust, authority, or cultural identity.
meaningVi: xói mòn; làm suy yếu dần (niềm tin, giá trị)
existingExample: Persistent corporate tax scandals tend to erode citizens' confidence in democratic institutions.

definitionEn: A set of moral principles guiding the behaviour and values of an individual, profession, or society.
meaningVi: hệ giá trị đạo đức, tinh thần chuẩn mực
existingExample: A strong conservation ethic must be embedded in primary education to cultivate environmentally responsible citizens.

definitionEn: The specific arrangement, structure, or technical standard in which information or an event is presented.
meaningVi: định dạng, cấu trúc trình bày, hình thức tổ chức
existingExample: Transitioning university examinations to an open-book format encourages analytical reasoning over memorisation.

definitionEn: To establish an institution, organisation, or settlement, or to base an argument on a principle.
meaningVi: thành lập, sáng lập; đặt nền móng cho
existingExample: Philanthropic coalitions collaborated to found an independent research institute dedicated to clean water.

definitionEn: Existing as a permanent, essential, or inseparable characteristic of something.
meaningVi: vốn có, cố hữu, nội tại
existingExample: Critics warn that algorithmic recruitment software carries inherent biases inherited from historical hiring data.

definitionEn: A deep, clear, and accurate understanding of a complex phenomenon, problem, or human behaviour.
meaningVi: cái nhìn sâu sắc, sự thấu hiểu bản chất
existingExample: Archaeological excavations provide invaluable insight into ancient trade networks and urban sanitation.

definitionEn: Essential and necessary to make a system, process, or whole complete.
meaningVi: không thể thiếu, cấu thành thiết yếu
existingExample: Public libraries remain an integral part of civic life by offering free digital access to low-income residents.

definitionEn: Done with the hands or physical effort rather than by automated machinery or electronic systems.
meaningVi: thuộc về tay chân, thủ công (không tự động hóa)
existingExample: Advances in industrial robotics are steadily replacing repetitive manual tasks across automotive assembly lines.

definitionEn: Fully developed mentally, emotionally, or structurally, showing sound judgement or established stability.
meaningVi: trưởng thành, chín chắn; phát triển hoàn chỉnh
existingExample: Solar photovoltaics have evolved into a mature technology capable of undercutting coal-fired power plants.

definitionEn: To intervene neutrally between opposing parties to help resolve a dispute or bring about agreement.
meaningVi: hòa giải, làm trung gian điều tiết
existingExample: Independent international bodies are often called upon to mediate cross-border water-sharing disputes.

definitionEn: A channel, system, or material through which information, artistic expression, or effects are conveyed.
meaningVi: phương tiện truyền tải, môi trường trung gian
existingExample: Short-form video has emerged as the dominant medium for political campaigning among younger voters.

definitionEn: Relating to armed forces, defence operations, or warfare.
meaningVi: thuộc về quân sự, quân đội
existingExample: Many civilian breakthroughs, including GPS and the internet, originated from state-funded military research.

definitionEn: Of the smallest possible amount, degree, or impact.
meaningVi: tối thiểu, ở mức nhỏ nhất có thể
existingExample: Well-designed eco-resorts aim to leave minimal ecological disturbance on surrounding coral reefs.

definitionEn: Experienced, felt, or done equally by two or more parties toward each other.
meaningVi: lẫn nhau, song phương, cùng chia sẻ
existingExample: Bilateral trade agreements endure only when both economies perceive tangible mutual benefits.

definitionEn: An accepted standard, pattern of behaviour, or expectation regarded as typical within a group or society.
meaningVi: chuẩn mực xã hội, quy tắc thông lệ
existingExample: Flexible hybrid schedules have rapidly shifted from an unusual perk to an accepted workplace norm.

definitionEn: To share common areas, responsibilities, or time periods partially with another entity.
meaningVi: chồng chéo, giao thoa, trùng lặp một phần
existingExample: When municipal and national agencies overlap in jurisdiction, disaster relief efforts can become sluggish.

definitionEn: Accepting or allowing what happens without active participation, resistance, or critical engagement.
meaningVi: thụ động, tiếp nhận mà không chủ động tham gia
existingExample: Passive consumption of endless social media feeds correlates with reduced attention spans among teenagers.

definitionEn: A distinct part or share of a larger whole, budget, population, or serving.
meaningVi: một phần, khẩu phần, tỷ phần
existingExample: A substantial portion of household income in major financial capitals is absorbed by housing costs.

definitionEn: Preceding or done in preparation for a fuller, more decisive investigation, negotiation, or action.
meaningVi: sơ bộ, ban đầu, mang tính chuẩn bị
existingExample: Preliminary clinical findings indicate that the new vaccine significantly lowers hospitalisation rates.

definitionEn: An official system of rules, scientific procedures, or diplomatic conventions governing conduct or operations.
meaningVi: quy trình chuẩn, giao thức, nghị định thư
existingExample: Hospitals introduced stricter hygiene protocol guidelines to curb the spread of drug-resistant bacteria.

definitionEn: To improve an idea, method, or system by making precise incremental changes, or to purify a substance.
meaningVi: tinh chỉnh, hoàn thiện, lọc tinh
existingExample: Engineers continuously refine battery chemistry to increase electric vehicle range while lowering costs.

definitionEn: To make a rule, restriction, or control less strict, or to become less tense.
meaningVi: nới lỏng (quy định, kiểm soát); thư giãn
existingExample: Environmentalists cautioned lawmakers not to relax air-quality regulations during the economic slowdown.

definitionEn: To prevent someone or something from acting excessively or moving beyond controlled limits.
meaningVi: kiềm chế, kìm hãm, ngăn chặn
existingExample: Central banks raise interest rates primarily to restrain runaway inflation and cool overheated markets.

definitionEn: A dramatic, fundamental transformation in technology, society, economics, or political governance.
meaningVi: cuộc cách mạng, sự biến đổi triệt để
existingExample: The digital revolution has fundamentally reshaped how citizens access news, education, and public services.

definitionEn: Unable or unwilling to adapt, bend, or change in response to evolving circumstances.
meaningVi: cứng nhắc, thiếu linh hoạt, khắt khe
existingExample: Excessively rigid standardised curricula often stifle teachers' creativity and disregard individual learning paces.

definitionEn: A specific path taken from one place to another, or a method for achieving a particular outcome.
meaningVi: tuyến đường, lộ trình; con đường đạt mục tiêu
existingExample: Expanding dedicated bus routes across suburban districts offers a cost-effective remedy for peak-hour congestion.

definitionEn: A projected sequence of possible future events or conditions used for analysis and planning.
meaningVi: kịch bản, viễn cảnh giả định
existingExample: Climate scientists model a worst-case scenario in which Arctic sea ice vanishes entirely during summer months.
